## Context

A session's sub-agents as their own rows, found through the CLI's lifecycle hooks rather than by placing them anywhere. The milestone opened with an investigation whose rule was fixed before the evidence, because 'cannot be done' had to stay a permitted verdict.

## Done means

A session Mustur started reports its sub-agents: each one's task, its age, the tool it is in, and its output once it finishes.
The hook is installed per session on the command line Start builds, writing nothing to the owner's configuration and nothing into the checkout.
A command the adapter does not recognise is left exactly as given and shows no rows rather than failing to start.
A sub-agent's prompt and the session's transcript path are not kept: the log holds a projection, not the payload.
Rows belong to the session that spawned them — starting a session forgets the last one's.
A stop for a sub-agent that never started makes no row.
A launch that never produced a sub-agent does not label a later one.
A row leaves a tool when the sub-agent leaves it, rather than showing the last tool forever.
Rows reach an open tab over the session socket, and their ages move without a frame to move them.

## Verified against

The real CLI in a real tmux pane, and the committed captures in docs/investigations/0002-harness/.

End to end: a session started through the adapter carried the hook into its pane (checked with tmux list-panes '#{pane_start_command}'); two sub-agents launched into it rendered as two rows carrying their own tasks and their own final messages. The same run produced two SubagentStop events for work the hook never saw start, which make no rows — found here rather than reasoned about, and now a regression test.

Pairing: nine launch-to-start pairs across three runs of three same-type sub-agents, each sub-agent's own tool call as independent ground truth for which was which. Six agents produced ground truth; six paired correctly, none wrongly. The three that produced none answered without calling a tool, which count.py establishes by showing three launches, three starts and three stops against two tool calls per run. Re-derive both with python3 docs/investigations/0002-harness/score.py and count.py, which read the committed captures and need no CLI.

The 30-second pairing window is sized from those same captures: the pairs run 1.563s to 5.985s. A test asserts the window is wider than the slowest pair measured, so shrinking it to 'a few seconds' fails rather than silently stripping labels off correct rows.

PostToolUse carrying agent_id was verified before being relied on, and that run also caught the parent's own PostToolUse for its Agent call arriving with no agent_id — which would have queued every task description twice.

## Risks

The task label is the one inference in the package, and it can still be wrong: order-pairing inside a window narrows the failure without closing it, which is what the owner chose on MUS-Q-0026 and was told plainly. A row with nothing left to claim carries no task rather than borrowing one.

The tool hooks fire on every tool call in the session, so a busy session spawns two short-lived processes per call. Not measured under load.

Sub-agent rows are the first thing this surface's client layer models that is not the terminal (MUS-Q-0029), which widens the one exception to the server-rendered rule.
